Skills "belong in the development process".

## IC. ICAO / aviation phraseology analogy [K — from author knowledge, NOT fetched; verify against ICAO Annex 10/11, Doc 4444, Doc 9432 before any normative use]
- Standard words with fixed meanings: affirm, negative, roger (received, not yes), wilco, unable, standby, say again, verify, correction, disregard; avoid "OK".
- Readback/hearback: pilot reads back safety-critical items; controller must verify and correct. A readback nobody checks is theater.
- SID/STAR: published named procedures referenced by name in the clearance; reduce workload, pre-agreed details.
- Lost-communications procedures: predefined behavior when contact is lost. Missed approach/go-around: predefined at decision altitude, not improvised.
- Pilot-in-command authority: may deviate in emergency but must declare and report afterwards.
- Urgency tiers (pan-pan/mayday) with fixed handling.
- IFR (controlled, clearance, controller responsible for separation) vs VFR with FIS/AFIS (information only, no clearances, pilot responsible); IFR can be picked up in the air and cancelled.
- Mapping proposed: sketch = VFR+FIS; promote = pick up IFR clearance; stall/timeouts = lost-comms; retry cap = missed approach; override = declared deviation; closed vocabulary + readback for gate churn. Limits: phraseology exists for noisy voice; rigidity is justified by lives at stake; needs enforcement/training; agents follow prompts so vocabulary must be short.

## CV. "Caveman" prompting — measured
- Skill: https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman (~94k stars per https://enterprisedna.co/resources/ai-pulse/ai-pulse-2026-07-28-a-claude-code-skill-called-caveman-respond-in-terse-fragment/ ). Repo eval [P]: 3 arms (baseline, "Answer concisely", skill), 1 call/arm/prompt on Opus 5.5, tiktoken o200k_base output tokens, fidelity regex checks; claims 65% mean (22–87%) over 10 prompts; self-stated limits: tokenizer approximation, n=1, regex-only fidelity, no cross-model.
- Independent [P, summarized]: https://dev.to/nazecode/i-measured-the-viral-talk-like-a-caveman-token-saver-a-two-word-prompt-got-most-of-it-118a — one C# debugging task, n=3/variant: "Be concise." −28.7%, caveman −42.9%, ultra −63.6%; all correct; skill needs ~10 answers to break even vs two-word prompt.
- JetBrains [P, full page via Playwright]: https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/07/speak-to-ai-agents-like-cavemen-tosave-tokens/ (Denis Shiryaev). Harbor 0.17, Claude Code 2.1.200, claude-sonnet-5 effort low, SkillsBench 86/87 tasks, 3 runs, ~240 trials, ~$106. Arm B forced activation (ceiling). Output tokens: smoke 10 tasks k=1 −29.5%; 10 tasks k=3 −6.7%; full 86 (82 clean pairs) k=1 −8.5% (592k→542k). Quality: 64 tied, 10 skill higher, 8 lower, sign test p=0.82; mean score 0.326 vs 0.311. Cost: expected ~−10% but raw totals +11.6% ($40.60 vs $36.39) due to single task crossing 200k long-context tier ($8.29 vs $0.33). Lesson: "Never trust a k=1 eval."
- Others [S]: real coding tasks 14–21% (BetterStack); community reproductions 30–50%; agentic ~8.5%; "Be concise. Return JSON." handles ~60% of savings.
- Brevity paper [S]: arXiv 2604.00025 "Brevity Constraints Reverse Performance Hierarchies in Language Models" — 31 models, 1,485 problems; brevity improves large-model accuracy up to 26 points on some benchmarks; Concise-CoT study [S, unverified] showed GPT-3.5 −27.69% on math.

## RT. rtk (Rust Token Killer) — JetBrains test [P, full page via Playwright]
- https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/07/rtk-claude-code-token-savings/ (Part 2, Jul 20 2026). Harbor 0.18, Claude Code 2.1.201, claude-sonnet-5 at low and high effort, rtk v0.43.0 as `rtk init -g` ships (binary + PreToolUse hook + RTK.md), 425 trials, ~$320.
- Claimed −60–90%. Ceiling analysis from replay of 83 transcripts: of 1,056 shell commands, 349 rewritable, 525 no rule (python3, project scripts, loops), 182 skipped on purpose; of 1.9M chars tool output, 20% compressible, 46% shell without rule, 34% Read/Grep bypassing hook; total cap ≈3% of input.
- Measured: low effort, 80 clean pairs: cost +7.6% median (p=0.004), turns +13.8% (p=0.03), cache reads +14.3% (p=0.008), fresh input +3.2% (p=0.23), output +6.7% (ns); heavily-rewritten pairs +24% vs +5%. High effort: cost +0.1% (p=0.99). Quality: 151 paired tasks 10 better/8 worse/133 identical; sign test p=1.0 both efforts. One compatibility failure (glibc) and one broken rewrite class (compound find predicates). `rtk gain` reported 96.2M tokens saved while the bill rose: counterfactual counts raw output (1.2MB cat = 320k "saved"), chars÷4 estimate, cached re-reads at a tenth of price.
- Lessons: "a tool's self-reported savings are a claim about its counterfactual, not about your bill"; paired analysis only; per-task medians + Wilcoxon; exclude errored tasks from both arms; ladder: free transcript replay → wiring check → k=1 smoke → k=3 → full run at each effort. ~80 tasks can only rule out large effects (~700 runs/side for subtle shifts). User's global config (~/.claude/RTK.md) installs rtk with the same hook — an own-workflow paired test is an open item; do not change user config without being asked.

## NF. Netflix + JetBrains IDE intelligence — https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/10/how-netflix-made-ai-coding-agents-more-efficient/ (Oct 15 2026) [P, full page; vendor-hosted case study]

Netflix built the daemon (keeps index warm, session manager by project root, GraalVM executable) and CLI because the LSP alone isn't callable by an agent.

# Repository Hooks

These hooks apply only while working in `orin-dx/wisp-plugins`. They are project configuration, not distributable plugin behavior.

## Commit-time integrity guard

Claude and Codex run `scripts/authoring-integrity-hook.py` before a shell command that invokes `git commit`. The hook is silent unless it blocks a commit for one of two hard invariants:

- A tracked `shared/schemas/<name>@<version>.json` file is modified, deleted, renamed, or copied instead of adding a new version.
- The generated Codex marketplace artifacts (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `dist/codex`) do not exactly match the authored Codex sources and catalog.

The hook does not run tests, rewrite files, add context, inspect ordinary edits, or act outside this repository. It permits new schema files and reports the one corrective action when it blocks.

## Configuration

| Harness | Configuration | Hook command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Claude Code | `.claude/settings.json` | `PreToolUse` for `Bash` |
| Codex | `.codex/hooks.json` | `PreToolUse` for `Bash` |

Both harness adapters invoke the same standard-library Python check and accept its shared `{"decision":"block","reason":"..."}` output. The adapters remain separate because each harness resolves project-root paths and hook configuration independently.

## Verification

Run the hook test with:

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests/test_authoring_integrity_hook.py -v
```

To inspect or trust the Codex hook, use `/hooks`. Claude Code exposes its configured hooks through its `/hooks` view.

input.content:
# Front-end and design-ideation evaluation of the Wisp plugins

Status: proposal and evidence base. No plugin, schema, constitution or ADR was changed by this work. Every change below is a work package (WP) awaiting a decision.

## Why this exists

The plugins were used on two brand sites (techworx and orin-dx). This evaluation reads the sessions and repos from that work, surveys how the industry does agentic design and front-end work, and turns both into a sequenced plan. The trigger was a user observation: the plugin workflows are too rigid for early, experimental, idea-flushing work, where the goal is to see designs and check that tools work without specs, tests or gates.

## Contents

| Path | What it is |
| :-- | :-- |
| `CATALOG.md` | The plan: 144 work packages, a dependency graph, six waves, 10 proposed ADRs, 20 conflicts with resolutions, and post-verification amendments (section 5) |
| `traceability/` | Five matrices mapping about 1,000 individual findings to WPs, each with contradictions, claims to verify, and proposed new WPs. `WP-draft.md` is the first draft the matrices were built against |
| `verification/` | `VERIFY-1.md` (transcript and repo claims) and `VERIFY-2.md` (web and documentation claims). They correct errors in the evidence notes |
| `evidence/` | The raw research notes. Index and tag legend in `evidence/README.md` |

Read in this order: this file, then `CATALOG.md` sections 3 to 5, then `verification/`, then a matrix when you need the source of a specific WP.

## What the sessions show

Scope: about 812 transcript files, but only a handful are real top-level sessions; the rest are subagent transcripts. Plugin agents were used in two sessions: `orin-dx` b8d16e96 (09-29 to 10-03) and `pages` 24655582 (10-05 to 10-16). `vanguard` ran once, on 10-17, for blog-topic research. Everything else, including nearly all design ideation, used no plugin.

1. **Strong on behavior, blind on appearance.** Gates caught real contradictions, accessibility values (a 2.82:1 contrast failure recomputed from the token source), and cross-spec conflicts. Every visible defect was found by a human look, an audit, or the 16 Oct suite. `spec@1` has no way to express visual intent and nothing renders anything.
2. **Gate loops were fix-and-resubmit.** 38 gate calls in the `orin-dx` session (28 muse, 10 scribe) and 51 `muse:exit-gate` calls in the `pages` session (per spec: 7, 5, 6, 9, 4, 6, 8, 6 for SPEC-005 to 012, inside a 57-minute window). Every spec failed its first gate with 9 to 23 blockers. The retry cap of 3 was not enforced: gates said "escalate" from retry 4 and the orchestrator continued with no user message in between (SPEC-005 ended at retry 6, SPEC-008 at 9). All eight specs finished as passes with empty blockers.
3. **Approval in prose failed.** The user asked to see rendered examples at least seven times and the agent described first each time. Drawn prototypes then exposed a touch-target bug the gated spec missed.
4. **Specs lagged the design.** Specs gated on 11 Oct were rewritten the next day after decisions made from drawn pages, and the 12 Oct revisions ran with "no exit gate this round". SPEC-013 supersedes much of SPEC-001 and SPEC-003c.
5. **Exploration worked best outside the plugins.** Option boards (Artifacts in Oct, repo-script Playwright screenshots, local pages) and short answer codes. The user stated the two-phase model explicitly on 2026-10-14 at 20:25 UTC (`pages` line 49946): exploratory build quick, specs and tests when it narrows. The same session built the landing, Tools and Principles pages in about 30 minutes once the audit machinery stopped.
6. **Ceremony still paid off for stable contracts.** The SiteNav migration passed 478 Chromium e2e tests, and the challenger found real plan defects.
7. **Defects shipped past the gates** (confirmed in git history): "NaN%" glass opacity on the Orin brand page, card strand fades that cut hard at phone width, tool marks stretched and 2px low, colour-card labels at 2.9 to 4.3:1 contrast, a filter 1px short of the 44px target, duplicate banner landmarks, and misattributed decisions in case-study copy.
8. **Stalls and unused agents.** The `orin-dx` session had 17 failed agent tasks (11 watchdog stalls, 6 API errors); the `pages` session had none. `smith:recon` and every `sentinel:*` agent appear in no transcript, `smith:reviewer`, `smith:mutator` and `smith:exit-gate` ran only in a third project, and the cause is unknown (WP-56).

## What the plugins lack, by design

- No browser, screenshot, Storybook or visual capability anywhere; the `workspace-manifest@1` capability list is closed and cannot record one.
- No schema for a direction, brief, wireframe, prototype, copy deck or critique, and no divergent cognitive mode.
- Muse's docs point three times to "ranger's accessibility hazard taxonomy"; ranger has none, so implemented accessibility is never checked (WP-01, WP-44).
- Every build path runs recon, mutation, review and a binding exit-gate; there is no spike or sketch mode. Constitution rules (default-fail gates, no TBDs) make an unfinished idea an invalid artifact.
- 29 of 31 schemas carry a mandatory `reasoning` scratchpad field (constitution line 242). Anthropic's refusals documentation names exactly this pattern as a `reasoning_extraction` trigger on the current Claude 5 tiers, with no fallback model and billed pre-output refusals. Whether it fires for Wisp's schemas is untested, so WP-61 tests before any rename.

## What the industry shows

Corrected after verification; see `verification/VERIFY-2.md` for evidence.

- **Intent and behavior are separate artifacts** (DESIGN.md, uSpec, Storybook, Atlassian). `spec@1` mixes them and can express only behavior.
- **Extract deterministically, then let the model add judgment** (uSpec; Netflix and JetBrains code intelligence; Spectrum's generated skills). It maps to the stale-number problem in the specs.
- **Render, then compare** is the standard verification loop, and Anthropic's own guidance recommends giving the agent a way to verify its work. A clean axe run covers about 57% of accessibility issues by volume (Deque, 2021).
- **Lint is the preferred gate** (Salesforce, Primer, Spectrum, Vercel). Gates that only judge text miss rendered defects.
- **Mode routing separates exploring from hardening** (Vercel's product-design skill: shape, implement, review, copy, harden; exploration modes make no edits).
- **A monolithic DESIGN.md is costly:** Atlassian measured 7.21M tokens against 3.75M for MCP, 4.43M for a skill and 4.20M for no context on one task. Vercel's design.md showed 39 vs 91 failures but on six pages, so it is weak evidence either way. Use a small routed intent file and lookups, and run our own paired test (WP-402).
- **Nobody has a real decision log.** Claude Design has no version history and Figma Make users ask for branching.
- **Token-saving prompts and tools do little in agentic work.** Caveman: about 8.5% output tokens on 82 paired tasks with no detectable quality change (JetBrains, Sonnet 5 at low effort, a ceiling because activation was forced). rtk: no token saving and a +7.6% cost at low effort (p=0.004), none at high effort; its own `rtk gain` scoreboard reported 96.2M tokens saved while the bill rose. The method is the reusable part: paired runs, medians, bill-based, failures excluded from both arms, and never trusting k=1.
- **Corrections from verification:** 15 of 21 design systems ship `llms.txt` (not "almost none"); Coinbase's Code Connect figures are +1 quality point, -29.5% tokens and -19.6% duration over 27 tasks on two design systems; v0 Design Systems 2.0 launched 2026-06-25; the Figma Starter limit is 20 calls per month; `test-run` is the Storybook MCP tool name; WCAG 2.5.8 is AA at 24x24 and the 44x44 figure is 2.5.5 at AAA; Codex custom agents are natively TOML (repo policy still keeps role cards markdown).
- **Not found:** first-party Airbnb or Netflix design-system AI material (Netflix's JetBrains case study concerns Java code intelligence), and verified Shopify design-rules material. These are dispositions in the matrices, not silent omissions.

## The plan

144 work packages, none dropped. Eight overlap another WP and are merged into it with a reason; about 20 more overlap and are kept with the reason stated. Full table in `CATALOG.md`.

| Wave | Theme | WPs | Needs first |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 0 | Defects, baselines, measurement | 21 | nothing |
| 1 | Exploration modes (the stated priority) | 19 | ADR N1 |
| 2 | Gate hygiene and orchestration | 27 | ADR N4, N5 |
| 3 | Visual intent and evidence | 43 | ADR N2, N3 (one schema bundle) |
| 4 | Prompt, model, Codex, AGENTS.md, distribution | 27 | ADR N8, N9, N10 (conditional) |
| 5 | Consumer-repo and research follow-ups | 7 | nothing |

Highlights:
- **Wave 0:** fix the muse dangling reference and move muse to `verdict@3`; baseline the gate metrics from transcripts; build the paired-eval harness; test the `reasoning` refusal risk first (WP-61); find why agents went unused (WP-56).
- **Wave 1:** a mode router (shape, sketch, spike, implement, review, copy, harden, promote); a `sketch` skill with durable option files (stable ids, status, one-line reason) that double as the decision log, rendered locally as a brand x theme x viewport matrix, TBDs allowed, no gate; a smith `spike` skill to check that a tool or library works; a show-first rule; direction-commit and anti-slop controls; a lightweight promote (WP-14a) that carries a chosen option forward as a requirement plus a brief.
- **Wave 2:** evidence-citing blockers, "no findings" as a valid pass, enforced retry caps with logged overrides, readback in correction loops, a small fixed vocabulary, stall procedures, orchestrator-owned spawning, and file ownership for parallel work.
- **Wave 3:** `spec@2` with token and visual references, a render-evidence artifact and manifest capability, deterministic UI checks (tokens, contrast, target size, landmarks, copy provenance), the full promote path, a visual critic, and ground-truth extraction before drafting.
- **Wave 4:** ablations of the constitution and prompt structure measured net of cache hits, tier re-checks per model, Codex role cards, an AGENTS.md strategy, and skill versioning and maintenance.

Design choices made in the catalog's conflict table (section 4): 3 options per round and 4 directions only at the first direction-commit; 3 parallel writers by default and up to 5 for disjoint work; scanners report everything and a separate stage filters while gates stay scoped to stated requirements (test first in WP-60); no tier changes on vendor claims until measured (WP-63).

## How the user's guidance is covered

| Guidance | Where |
| :-- | :-- |
| Flexible, "vibe-coded" exploration without worrying about specs and tests | Wave 1: WP-10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19; mode router gives each mode its own gate set (conflict K12) |
| See designs | WP-12 (rendered option matrix, local first), WP-211 (show-first rule), WP-34 |
| Validate that tools work | WP-15 smith `spike`: smoke-check evidence, verified-vs-unverified report, promote or discard |
| Specs and tests once ideas narrow, without regressions | WP-14a/b promote, WP-19 harden, WP-106 to 108 spec hygiene, WP-204 test taxonomy |
| Do not cut things | 144 WPs, 8 merged with reasons, dispositions for items with no action; nothing was dropped |
| Learn from industry, model vendors, AGENTS.md, uSpec, ICAO, TanStack Intent | Waves 3 and 4; WP-32 and 33 (uSpec), WP-71 (AGENTS.md), WP-53, 54 and 212 (ICAO ideas), WP-72 (Intent) |

## Open items and limits

- **Unverified here:** pages commit counts (git was blocked for that repo), the `a859e2f` origin claim, the 271 KB JS budget, whether SPEC-013 supersedes 26 of SPEC-001's and 35 of SPEC-003c's criteria, Shopify and Airbnb figures, the Figma 25k response cap, GPT-6 effort `none`, Atlassian's earlier 34% and 16% figures, and the ICAO terminology (written from knowledge, not fetched; check Annex 10/11 and Docs 4444 and 9432 before any normative use).
- **Weak evidence by nature:** vendor self-benchmarks and small samples (Vercel's six pages, Atlassian's single task). WP-401 proposes tagging them.
- **One project:** all transcript evidence is from two sessions in one body of work. Gate cost in tokens and time was not measured (WP-03, WP-91).
- **Not read:** several Anthropic engineering posts and Claude Code pages, OpenAI launch and system-card pages that returned 403, and uSpec's repository contents.
- **User configuration untouched:** `~/.claude/RTK.md` installs rtk with the same hook JetBrains tested. Whether it helps this workflow is an open paired test (WP-68), not a recommendation to change it.

## Next decisions

1. Accept or amend the wave order, in particular Wave 1 before Wave 2.
2. Write ADR N1 (exploratory mode, amending ADR 003) and N6 (the `reasoning` field), and run the WP-61 refusal test.
3. Decide whether sketch and promote live as skills in `muse` (which already owns UI) or in a new plugin; `AGENTS.md` allows several skills in one plugin when intents are heterogeneous, and the catalog assumes `muse`.

I've turned the research into a verified, committed evidence base and a plan of 144 work packages with nothing dropped. The branch is not pushed: the permission classifier denied `git push` as an out-of-place publication, and I didn't try another route.

I checked the work by running `just check`, which passes: 49 tests, version agreement, and all 21 mermaid blocks including the dependency graph. The repo's reference-integrity test also caught the proposed new reference files, which I marked `<refs>/` so they aren't treated as broken. No plugin, schema, constitution or ADR was changed.

## Where it lives
- **Path:** `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/`
- **Branch:** `worktree-frontend-design-evaluation`, committed locally as `c2c1b05b`
- **Worktree:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/wisp-plugins/.claude/worktrees/frontend-design-evaluation`
- **Start with:** `README.md`, then `CATALOG.md` sections 3 to 5, then `verification/`. `traceability/` holds five matrices of about 1,000 mapped findings, and `evidence/` has the raw notes.

## What "don't cut things" produced
- **Everything is traced.** Each finding maps to a work package or has an evidence-based disposition, such as "no public material found". Eight overlapping work packages are merged into another with reasons stated, and none were deleted or renumbered.
- **Your rigidity point now leads the plan.**
  - Wave 1 (exploration modes) comes right after Wave 0 (defects, baselines, measurement), ahead of gate hygiene.
  - It covers a mode router, a `sketch` skill with a decision log, a smith `spike` skill for checking that tools work, and a lightweight promote.
  - It needs only one new ADR, N1. Full `spec@2` and render evidence come later, in Wave 3.
- **Verification corrected several earlier figures:**
  - The "296 tests pinned the wrong constant" claim was unsupported and is dropped.
  - "32 stalled" was not reproducible. The `orin-dx` session had 17 failed agent tasks and the `pages` session had none.
  - 384 of 1116 tests is the plan's classification, not a confirmed deletion count.
  - "Almost none ship `llms.txt`" was wrong. 15 of 21 design systems do.
  - The Coinbase figures I quoted and the v0 launch date were also wrong.
- **Decision-changing finding:** Anthropic's refusals page names a `reasoning` field in JSON as a documented refusal trigger. 29 of 31 Wisp schemas require one. I didn't run the test, so WP-61 does that before anyone renames anything.

## Decisions for you
1. **Push the branch,** or tell me where you'd prefer it, and whether to open a draft PR. I left both alone.
2. **Accept or change the wave order.** In particular, confirm that Wave 1 (exploration) goes before Wave 2 (gate hygiene).
3. **Sketch and promote in `muse`, or a new plugin?** The catalog assumes `muse`.
4. **Write ADR N1 (exploratory mode) and N6 (the `reasoning` field) next,** and run the WP-61 refusal test first.

Left unchecked: your pages commit counts and some Shopify and Airbnb figures, the ICAO terminology (written from knowledge, not fetched), and the untried `rtk` question for your own workflow. Your `~/.claude/RTK.md` is untouched.
